html:
SMTO-CMP-0032 — Your newer message arrived before the AI finished

GUID: 6a22898c-0075-4684-a3d9-43a7484a3909
Slug: completion-superseded-intent
Domain: CMP · Subsystem: cmp

What happened

  • You sent a new instruction while the AI was finishing this task. SMTO set the AI's finish aside so it can follow your latest instruction instead. Work already done is kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Let the task keep running. The AI now follows your latest message together with the original request. SMTO wants the finished task to match what you asked for most recently.
  2. When it finishes, check that the reply covers your latest message, not just the original request. Your newer instruction may change what the right result is.
  3. If it missed your update, send another message restating what you want. Don't ask it to repeat earlier changes that already worked. Restating keeps the task on track without redoing finished steps.

What success looks like

  • The task finishes as Completed and the reply reflects your latest message.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Open Technical details, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't restart the task from the beginning; earlier changes would run again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Direct completion was rejected because the run store holds user amendments newer than the run's captured amendment_seq, so the completion no longer reflects the current task intent.

What this means

  • Before direct completion, the store has user amendments beyond the run's captured amendment sequence. Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.

Why this can happen

  • Before direct completion, the store has user amendments beyond the run's captured amendment sequence.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the current accepted amendment and reassess its requirements against retained results.

How to fix it

  • Read the pending amendments for the run (store.amendments after amendment_seq) and let the amendment flow rebind the output policy and recovery state. The model must reassess the latest accepted intent against existing results before completing; do not replay earlier mutations.
  • Use the current accepted user intent and its output requirements.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Completion addresses the latest accepted intent and output requirements.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Completion checks consume retained evidence and the effective guard policy; they do not execute work. A rejected declaration preserves the answer and successful receipts, and only the original operation evidence establishes effects.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
